question: Turisti v Slovenskom raji či v Tatrách chodia na „ferraty“. Pomenovanie via ferrata pochádza z taliančiny. Čo doslova znamená?

extra.why_interesting: Slovaks hear 'ferrata' as just a sport label and never translate it. Once they hear the meaning, the steel cables, rungs and ladders they have gripped suddenly explain the name. Anyone who knows 'ferrum' or 'Ferrari-like' Italian words can reason their way to it.
extra.verification_notes: Merriam-Webster gives the literal meaning as 'iron path/road', which matches 'Železná cesta'; the 'via attrezzata' etymology is a minority view that doesn't change the literal translation.

explanation: Názov odkazuje na oceľové laná, kramle a rebríky pripevnené do skaly. Preslávili sa v Dolomitoch počas prvej svetovej vojny, keď nimi vojaci sprístupňovali horské hrebene.

question: V roklinách Slovenského raja, napríklad v Suchej Belej, sa po rebríkoch a reťaziach popri vodopádoch smie ísť iba jedným smerom. Ktorým?
source_excerpt: Search summary: the ravine is one-way and starts from the Podlesok campsite (uphill only); exact page wording not retrieved.

extra.why_interesting: Many players have walked these gorges without registering that the direction is mandated. Those who haven't can reason it out: narrow ladders over waterfalls make passing impossible, and climbing up a wet ladder is much safer than going down it. That gives an 'I can work this out' moment.
extra.verification_notes: Travel guides and a geocache page say Suchá Belá is one-way, uphill only, from Podlesok; I found no official park page and no sign the rule has changed.

explanation: Rokliny sú jednosmerné, takže sa smie len stúpať proti prúdu. Na úzkych mokrých rebríkoch by sa ľudia nemali ako vyhnúť a zostupovať po nich dolu je oveľa nebezpečnejšie.
